title: Cannot connect to IBM i — port 449 blocked
root_cause: IBM i host servers communicate over port 449 (central server / sign-on service). When a firewall rule, network policy, or IBM i subsystem QUSRWRK is not active, outbound or inbound connections on port 449 are refused, preventing any IBM i client (Code for IBM i, ACS, JDBC) from completing the sign-on handshake.
resolution_steps: Verify port 449 is open on the network firewall between your workstation and the IBM i system: run 'Test-NetConnection <ibmi-host> -Port 449' in PowerShell.
On the IBM i system, confirm the QUSRWRK subsystem is active: WRKACTJOB SBS(QUSRWRK).
Start the host servers if not running: STRHOSTSVR SERVER(*ALL).
Confirm the sign-on server is listening: NETSTAT *CNN, look for port 449 in LISTEN state.
If behind a corporate VPN, confirm IBM i traffic is routed through the VPN tunnel and not split-tunnelled away.
suggested_approach: Ensure QUSRWRK subsystem is active and host servers are started via STRHOSTSVR SERVER(*ALL). If a firewall is blocking port 449, the network or firewall configuration needs to be updated to allow TCP traffic on port 449 between client workstations and the IBM i system. No code change to Code for IBM i is expected to be required for this issue.

title: Stuck at 'Starting Mapepire' after upgrading to Code for IBM i 3.x
root_cause: After upgrading to Code for IBM i 3.x, the extension attempts to start the Mapepire database server (NOXDBSRV). If a previous Mapepire job is still active from an older version — or if the NOXDBSRV service program objects on the IBM i system are stale or locked — the startup sequence hangs indefinitely waiting for the server to respond. The extension does not time out gracefully in this state.
resolution_steps: Open an IBM i terminal session and run: WRKACTJOB JOB(NOXDB*) to identify any stuck Mapepire jobs.
End any stuck jobs found: ENDJOB JOB(<job-number>/QUSER/NOXDBSRV) OPTION(*IMMED).
Clear any object locks on NOXDBSRV: WRKOBJLCK OBJ(QGPL/NOXDBSRV) OBJTYPE(*SRVPGM).
In VS Code, run the command 'Code for IBM i: Disconnect' then reconnect to the IBM i system.
If the hang persists, delete and reinstall the Mapepire server objects: in Code for IBM i, open the command palette and run 'Code for IBM i: Install Mapepire'.
Restart VS Code if the status bar still shows 'Starting Mapepire' after reconnecting.
validation_commands: SELECT JOB_NAME, JOB_STATUS, ELAPSED_TIME FROM TABLE(QSYS2.ACTIVE_JOB_INFO()) WHERE JOB_NAME LIKE '%NOXDB%'
suggested_approach: The root cause appears to be that Code for IBM i 3.x does not gracefully handle a pre-existing or stale NOXDBSRV job on the IBM i system when initiating the Mapepire connection. A suggested fix would be to add a startup check in the Mapepire connection logic that: (1) queries QSYS2.ACTIVE_JOB_INFO() for any existing NOXDB* jobs before attempting to start a new server instance, (2) either reuses the existing job if it is healthy or ends it cleanly before starting fresh, and (3) implements a configurable timeout with a user-visible error message rather than hanging indefinitely. This approach is AI-proposed — Code for IBM i maintainers should verify against the actual Mapepire startup code before implementation.
